The last confirmed structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, supports that reading - NQ futures settled at 30,148.25, down 40.25 points or 0.13%, mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band, while the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14 (-0.13%) about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%) and the latest H.15 showing 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%. Stress stays elevated at 45% because the backdrop is not calm: the Strait of Hormuz remains shut with Iran tying any reopening to sanctions relief and war reparations, tanker attacks have halted traffic outright, WTI settled at $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent at $88.52 (+1.67%) for a weekly gain above 5%, and Friday's U.S. consumer data was sharply soft - Retail Sales -0.6% against +0.1% expected and Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5. recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (9%) alone. No venue is quoting NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint is the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, where a full weekend of accumulated headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure - the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. Gap risk is genuinely two-way: Iran and Oman are reported close on a strait arrangement, yet Tehran conditions any reopening on an end to the U.S. naval blockade plus sanctions relief and war reparations, while Washington threatens an indefinite blockade and tells Americans to expect higher pump prices. Either thread can move crude before equities can price it, and Friday's weak consumer prints leave a second, unrelated growth-scare channel open into next week's FOMC minutes. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: Third night of the CME weekend halt leaves NQ with no live price path anywhere in the 24-hour horizon: Tail holds low at 9% and EA_ON, while Stress stays elevated at 45% on an unresolved Hormuz closure, a 5%+ weekly crude rally to $82.40 WTI, and Friday's sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses.
body:
No live price path is available this hour. CME equity-index futures closed for the weekend at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable for the whole of the current 24-hour horizon (04:00 UTC on 15 August to 03:00 UTC on 16 August). Everything below is the last confirmed state plus corroborated news re-verified from primary sources this hour, and that limitation - not a judgement that markets are calm - is what caps Confidence below the solid band.

Last confirmed structure, re-verified this hour: NQ futures settled at 30,148.25, down 40.25 points or 0.13% from a 30,188.50 prior settlement, inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 session band on 397,964 contracts (Investing.com). The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13% against a 30,084.50 previous close, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20 (Yahoo Finance). Both the futures and the cash index therefore finished mid-range on a small down day with two-way trade - not a persistent one-way liquidation, and not a close pinned to a session extreme. Nothing in that structure resembles the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension pattern that would justify Tail above the low band, which is why Tail stays at 9% rather than being lifted by the volatility backdrop alone.

Cross-asset: VIX closed at 14.25, down 2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and far below its 35.30 52-week high - equity volatility is not corroborating the geopolitical stress. The latest Federal Reserve H.15 (released 14 August, data for 13 August) shows the 2-year constant maturity at 4.15%, the 10-year at 4.63% and the 30-year at 5.21%; the curve is positively sloped and there is no yield shock aligned with the oil move. Crude is the one aligned amplifier: WTI settled at $82.40, up 1.42% on the day and more than 5% on the week, with Brent at $88.52, up 1.67% - crude snapped a two-week losing streak on the Hormuz impasse while the IEA warned of a deepening supply deficit. An oil-only amplifier with VIX at 14 and yields quiet is a Stress input, not a Tail input; the conflict between those signals is precisely why Stress sits well above Tail.

Geopolitics, the dominant live thread: the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut, with shipping described as subdued through the week and weakening further into the weekend, and tanker attacks reported as halting traffic outright. Iran and Oman are reported close to an arrangement, but Tehran's stated conditions for reopening are an end to the U.S. naval blockade, sanctions relief and war reparations - and Washington has threatened an indefinite blockade in response. The freshest wire, timed a few hours before this run, has Iran defiant on the strait while the U.S. administration tells Americans to accept high gasoline prices. This is a genuine unresolved second information wave into Sunday's reopen, and it is the main reason Stress does not decay through the weekend.

Macro: Friday's U.S. data was notably soft on the consumer. July Retail Sales came in at -0.6% month-on-month against a +0.1% consensus, the control group at -0.4% against +0.3%, and ex-autos at -0.3% against +0.2%; preliminary August Michigan Consumer Sentiment printed 51.0 against 54.5 expected. That is a second, independent risk channel that has nothing to do with the Gulf, and it will interact with the FOMC minutes on 19 August - the only high-impact scheduled U.S. event in the next seven days. Nothing at all is scheduled inside the current 24-hour horizon.

Synthesis: Tail 9% (low) is a statement that pathological one-way price-path risk cannot be observed, and cannot form, while no venue is quoting; the non-zero floor prices the discontinuity risk that a two-day headline gap carries into Sunday's open. Stress 45% (elevated) reflects a real and unresolved volatility backdrop - shut strait, crude up 5% on the week, soft consumer data, an active blockade standoff - none of which a market holiday neutralises. Confidence 59% (medium-low) is set by evidence quality, not by risk: levels, volatility, yields, crude, catalysts and the seven-day calendar are all fresh and primary-sourced, but the price path is missing entirely and only Sunday's reopen restores it. Dominant mode is mixed. The Jackson Hole symposium (27-29 August) and Nvidia's earnings (26 August) both sit outside the seven-day calendar window and are noted only as context.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 6-10% throughout. It held 9-10% through Friday's Asian and European sessions, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses and semiconductor weakness produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: roughly 25-29% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% has now held for five consecutive hours including this one. Those past opinions are preserved exactly as published. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and has firmed to 56-59% since midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 04:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 03:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly 19 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 9% for the first seventeen slots and ticking to 10% from 21:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to ease from 45% to about 41% through the thin Saturday Gulf, Asian and European hours, when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 45-46% into the late slots as unresolved threads converge on Sunday's price discovery: the Hormuz impasse and Tehran's reparations-and-sanctions conditions, the U.S. indefinite-blockade threat, the stalled Iran-Oman shipping talks, and a soft U.S. consumer picture heading into the 19 August FOMC minutes. Confidence stays in the medium-low band at 57-59% for as long as no venue quotes. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way, and the first live tape - not this forecast - is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.
